recipes.name: Cowgirl Cookies
ingredients_raw: 1 (3.5 ounce) jar coarsely chopped macadamia nuts

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease two cookie sheets.
Beat brown sugar, margarine, and white sugar together in a mixing bowl until light and fluffy. Beat in eggs, one at a time, until thoroughly blended. Stir in almond and vanilla extracts.

Stir flour, oats, baking soda, and salt together in a mixing bowl until well blended; stir into sugar mixture. Mix in coconut, white chocolate, and macadamia nuts until evenly blended. Drop dough by tablespoonfuls spaced 1 inch apart on the prepared cookie sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven until centers are set and edges are golden brown, about 15 minutes. Cool 3 minutes on cookie sheets before transferring to a wire rack to cool.

raw_recipe.headline: Cowgirl Cookies
raw_recipe.description: For this cowgirl cookies recipe, chunks of white chocolate, macadamia nuts, rolled oatmeal, and coconut make these hearty brown sugar cookies a favorite.

review.reviewBody: This is my recipe and I wanted to say that in the description it way the oven preheated, I wanted to say the cookie sheets preheated.

I made a trial run of these and cut the recipe in half just in case noone was a fan. I did the math for the sugars and did half and half of each so my cookies would be a lighter shade, like chocolate chip cookies. I also ground down the oatmeal in my blender to give it a less chunky consistancy. (We like our oatmeal cookies that way.) Instead of white chocolate chunks, I used white chocolate chips. The submitter suggested to preheat your cookie sheets but I found that just preheating the oven was sufficient. Ten minutes at 350* lent to a soft, chewy cookie. Heaven in your mouth. Next time I'll double the recipe and share with my friends and neighbors. This would be really good with Craisins, too, I think. Next time, I might use all vanilla.

Super cookies! I did not have vanilla or baking soda so I used 1 extra teaspoon of almond extract and substituted baking powder for the soda. Wonderful texture and flavor. With an "air-bake" cookie sheet I had to increase the baking time to 18 minutes and they are perfectly golden. These are now top of our list for cookies.

These were delicious and made so many! I made a few tweaks for preference—added pecans instead of macadamia nuts and switched the amounts for the vanilla and almond extracts; turned out great! Be aware: they spread a lot in the oven, so probably don’t do more than six to a sheet. Also, they didn’t need the whole fifteen minutes, twelve was the sweet spot for me, but of course it varies with the oven. I will make sure I never lose this recipe!

My kids made this recipe for a large family Christmas gathering. We typically make Cowboy Cookies, thought we'd try something different. The dough was a perfect consistency and they baked beautifully. We like chewy cookies, so we pulled our cookies out at 12 minutes and let them sit on the pan for two minutes. And this recipe truly makes 4 1/2 cookies, but they didn't last long. Fabulous Cookie!! Baking a batch again today!
I followed the recipe with the exception of substituting chopped pecans for macadamia nuts since I had none. But everyone who tasted the cookies loved them. I will definitely make them again

The almond extract was very dominant and ruined these cookies for me. I pulverized the oatmeal and coconut prior to adding it to the dry ingredients. They were also a bit too sweet. If I were to make them again I would leave out the almond extract.

We made these for our family holiday cookie baking day and they were a HUGE hit. I used all vanilla rather than vanilla and almond extract and they were delicious. The recipe makes a lot of cookies too which was great. 
Thanks for sharing!!

Amazing cookie! I love white chocolate macadamia cookies, and this is my favorite recipe! I blend my oats because I prefer the texture, used white chocolate chips, and left out the coconut, but those are just personal preferences. Some reviews suggest halfing the recipe, I think you can't have enough of these! I did and ended up with 26 large cookies. Delicious!

Delicious!! I didn't have macadamia nuts, so I used cashews. Note that this makes a very large batch. I was overflowing my KitchenAid! Next time I will make a half batch. This time I froze half the cookie dough.
Love these cookies! I had to make a change though as I can't eat any kind of chocolate. I used vanilla chips instead and they are easy to make, the recipe makes a ton, and they taste INCREDIBLE!

We really like these chewy cookies.

The first time I made these Cowgirl Cookies I followed the directions to a tee and they turned out wonderfully. Next time I think I will decrease the baking time from 15 minutes to 13 minutes to try for a little softer cookie.
Had no coconut and still awesome. You can't go wrong
Excellent and awesome

From the very first time I made this cookie, it has been a HIT! People who don't like white chocolate LOVE this cookie. People who don't like coconut, LOVE this cookie. Hands down - everyone LOVES this cookie!
My whole family couldn't get enough of these cookies! Thanks for the recipe, they were great!
LOVED these. Didn't change anything and they were perfect.
Delicious! 'Nuff said.
